svg.title: blueprint card: host-disk-saturation / anomaly_disk_aggressive_steady_r1
svg.desc: host-disk-saturation on run anomaly_disk_aggressive_steady_r1 (sockshop): fires. The gap between the nearest other fault and this one is 1.55x. This run measured 719.1 requests/s per x on "disk requests gained per unit of interrupt rise"; the cut is at 450.0. The fault that comes closest to breaking this cut is svc_mem_cap on trainticket at 352.4. This number alone: 10 of 272 runs land on the wrong side. Every gate together: 262 of 272 runs correct. disk requests per unit of interrupt rise: pass (719.1 needs > 450.0) FIRED host-disk-saturation - stress-ng-hdd arrived on the disk with 1956 more requests/s, 719 per unit of interrupt rise, while per-request service time stayed at 0.88x - a flood, no cpu-contention-co-tenant - thief None 0.0 cores, host 0.563 - does not match a bounded co-tenant workload no db-latency-dependency-wait - no socket-waiting syscall reached 5.0x (best 1.18x); on a fleet where many services share one process name this view averages the blocked service into no host-cpu-saturation - host CPU at 0.563, below the 0.95 ceiling no network-path-degradation - worst retransmission 0.0% is below the 12.0% bar no service-cpu-throttle - utilisation ratio 1.075, thief 0.0 cores, biggest loss -0.0832, runqueue 2.91x - not a quota holding work back no service-memory-cap - interrupt time 2.72x is raised, but 719 disk requests per unit of it is the flood shape - the pressure reached the device, so this is the disk
